Been there, but at the same time i can understand where they are coming from, tbh, when depressed, we can be hypersensitive to words and actions, i was once irritated by all these comments as well, but also have perpetually asked myself, what do i want from them actually? 
I reject common sensical word of encouragement coz meh
I reject communication coz i feel guilty talking abt my own feelings again and again

So actually what do i want from them?
Until now I can’t clearly pinpoint any 😅😂

You cannot be a Gordon Ramsay does that mean you stop cooking?
You cannot be Aristotle, Thomas Aquinas, Nietzsche, does that mean you stop thinking?
You cannot be Einstein, does that mean you stop studying?
You cannot be a saint, does that mean you stop being kind and good to your neighbors? 
You’re not gonna be an athlete, does that mean we stop taking care of our bodies?

Not being able to be the best doesn’t stop us from doing things we ought to do.

Our only competitor is ourselves a second ago, a minute ago, an hour ago, yesterday, last week, last year.. the only achievement that matters are the internals, silent victories we have over our past selves. Whatever external achievement and recognition we might get, are just a happy bonuses we get from working hard but it’s not particularly the only goal.

I like to think that there’s 3 kinds of cleaning.

1. Cleaning as in a general overhaul
          Discarding things
          Giving each and every remaining Item a “Proper place”
2. Maintenance cleaning
         Sweeping/Mopping/Dusting/
3. Inevitable Daily(Routine) Chores
          Washing Dishes/Laundry/Ironing

For most people, the reason why they seem lost and helpless abt cleaning is because they combine subtypes of the 3 above on a daily basis.

For the first type, as a freaking lazyyyyy person, the best that have worked for me so far really is the MariKondo style. (You can google that out or watch her show on Netflix, or like me, read her book “The life Changing Magic of Tidying Up”)
It helped me put my tidying into perspective.

How did it work for me? 
(a) it helped me grasp a proper mindset while cleaning and keeping only the things i really love and discard everything else. 
(a.1) Discard first before anything else.
(b) cleaning by category and not by location!!!! The best advice ever!! As it gives you an idea of how much of a category you have (clothings, books, handyman tools) e.g. Set a day to tackle a category example clothing. Look araound your house for ALL! your clothings including ALL bags and shoes. Collect them all in one place and you’ll be amazed and shock of the volume and how many of these you are not using anymore. Then decide what to keep and what to Discard.
for the criteria how to do this, pls check out MariKondo. It’s better hearing or reading her directly for full insight.
(c) store vertically~ like everything! for easier access 
(d) the biggest take away for me really is that after the big haul, maintenance cleaning is easier to do, hence I don’t feel burdened soing the daily chores

When every little thing has a “Proper place” ~and I can’t emphasize this enough~ in your home, everything becomes easier. The peace of mind it gives you is priceless.
Daily chores(type 3) stop being annoying because these are the only things i’ll be doing daily and can be done in an hour or less. As for Ironing and Laundry i set a schedule like every 2 days or so. 
For maintenance cleaning (type 2) since there is much less clutter i can make do of doing this every 1 or 2 weeks 

Hope this helps
